overrides.new: Elevated mechanical platform vs. at-grade mechanical yard

AccelDeck™ moves chillers and primary distribution above the data center — keeping grade-level circulation, walls, and site perimeter clean. The prefabricated platform organizes routing, access, embeds, and equipment support into one repeatable system for faster, more predictable installation.

Traditional at-grade chiller yards consume valuable site area and crowd the perimeter with exposed equipment, piping, headers, and field-built steel — increasing trade coordination, constraining access, and reducing flexibility for generators, electrical yards, and future expansion.

Traditional at-grade chiller yards consume valuable site area and crowd the perimeter with exposed equipment, piping, headers, and field-built steel — increasing trade coordination, constraining access, and reducing flexibility for generators, electrical yards, and future expansion.

unplaced: Beam profile and spacing accommodates most chiller models — giving owners flexibility to procure different chillers late in the manufacturing phase, even allowing future replacements without modifying the underlying support.
Standard configuration supports chiller, tanks, and equipment with weights up to 40,000 lbs. Design can be customized to accommodate more challenging configurations.
Fully compatible with Clark Pacific's AccelCore™ structural system, ensuring durability, longevity, and seamless integration with the overall project.
Simplifies pipe and equipment installations, creating flexible attachment points for hanging MEP and IT loads without field drilling.
Six foot plus heights provide easy access for maintenance and future equipment upgrades — planned from day one.
Factory-installed grating with moveable sections improves maintenance access in completed data centers.
Plant-installed, embedded strut-channel inserts support chilled-water piping, cable trays, and related mechanical equipment.
Incorporating AccelDeck™ into a prefabricated precast data center can reduce project timelines by months — an additional 4–8 weeks of schedule compression.
